prd.title: Character Extraction Improvements: Unnamed and Descriptive Characters
prd.target: Improve character extraction for books with unnamed or descriptively-referred characters

executive_summary: The character extraction pipeline is fundamentally designed around proper names, causing it to fail on important unnamed characters. This PRD addresses: (1) substring matching bugs causing pronouns like 'he' to appear as characters, (2) fragmentation of descriptive references like 'the creature'/'the monster'/'the wretch' into separate low-mention entries, and (3) lack of epithet alias resolution. The solution is book-agnostic and will improve extraction for any novel with unnamed antagonists, descriptive character handles, or recurring epithets.

current_failures.root_cause: No word boundaries in mention matching (llm.py:224-227)

current_failures.example: 'the creature' and 'the wretch' as separate 2-mention characters
current_failures.root_cause: LLM prompt explicitly excludes 'Generic titles without names' (line 41)
current_failures.impact: Unnamed antagonist split across many low-quality entries

current_failures.example: 'the monster', 'the fiend', 'the daemon' not recognized as same entity
current_failures.root_cause: Consensus alias resolution requires shared name components
current_failures.impact: Descriptive handles never merged, no usable profile generated

generalizes_to: Classics with unnamed entities ('the creature', 'the stranger', 'the governess')
Any book where major character is referenced via role/epithet more than proper name

features.name: Harden Mention Matching
features.rationale: Substring matching is the root cause of pronoun pollution. This single fix eliminates the worst false 'characters' and stabilizes mention counts.
features.current_behavior: llm.py _find_mentions() uses regex without word boundaries, causing 'he' to match inside 'the', 'whether', 'they'
features.proposed_behavior: Add word boundary markers (\b) and stopword filter for pronouns/determiners

user_stories.description: Pronouns are not extracted as characters
steps: Run analysis on a book with first-person narration
Examine character list in analysis.json
Verify 'he', 'she', 'it', 'they' do not appear as character names
Check that mention counts are reasonable (no 400+ mention characters that are pronouns)
Confirm character profiles are for actual characters

user_stories.description: Word boundary matching prevents substring matches
steps: Run analysis on a book containing 'the', 'whether', 'they' words
Verify 'he' does not match inside 'the' or 'whether'
Check that legitimate character names still match correctly
Confirm 'Victor' matches 'Victor' but not 'victory'

changes.description: Add word boundary markers to regex pattern
changes.after:
pattern = re.escape(name)
pattern = pattern.replace(r"\ ", r"\s+")
pattern = r'\b' + pattern + r'\b'

changes.description: Filter out stopwords after name extraction

features.name: Non-Proper-Name Character Handle Path
features.rationale: Allow extraction of recurring descriptive handles ('the creature', 'the detective') when they are agentive (speak/act) and appear multiple times.
features.current_behavior: LLM prompt explicitly says 'Do NOT include: Generic titles without names (the doctor, a woman)'
features.proposed_behavior: Update prompt to allow 'descriptive' character type for recurring, agentive definite descriptions

user_stories.description: Recurring descriptive handles are extracted as characters
steps: Run analysis on Frankenstein
Examine character list
Verify 'the creature' or similar descriptive handle appears as a character
Check that character has type='descriptive'
Confirm character has meaningful mention count (not fragmented)

user_stories.description: One-off generic roles are not extracted
steps: Run analysis on a book with incidental characters ('a waiter', 'some stranger')
Verify one-off generic roles do not appear as characters
Check that only recurring (3+) agentive descriptions are included
Confirm no pollution of character list with generic one-off mentions

user_stories.description: Descriptive handles must be agentive to be included
steps: Run analysis on a book with non-agentive descriptions ('the blue house', 'the old car')
Verify non-person descriptions are not extracted
Check that only descriptions that speak/act/are pursued are included
Confirm agentive detection uses dialogue and action verb patterns

changes.code:
class CharacterType(str, Enum):
    STORY = "story"
    HISTORICAL = "historical"
    REFERENCED = "referenced"
    DESCRIPTIVE = "descriptive"  # NEW
    UNCERTAIN = "uncertain"

@dataclass
class CharacterMention:
    text: str
    position: int
    chapter_index: int
    context: str
    in_dialogue: bool
    is_agentive: bool = False  # NEW

changes.summary: Update prompt to: (1) Allow 'descriptive' type for recurring epithets, (2) Require epithets to appear 3+ times AND be agentive, (3) Add 'acts' field to JSON response

features.name: Epithet Alias Resolution
features.rationale: Current consensus can't merge 'the creature' = 'the monster' = 'the wretch' because they share no name components. Need semantic alias resolution for epithets.
features.current_behavior: Alias resolution requires shared name words; epithets have no overlap
features.proposed_behavior: Add separate epithet alias resolution using LLM to identify semantic equivalence, with canonicalization preference for most specific/unique handle

steps: Run analysis on Frankenstein
Examine character list
Verify 'the creature', 'the monster', 'the wretch', 'the fiend' are aliases of ONE character
Check that canonical name is the most specific/unique form
Confirm merged character has combined mention count
Run analysis on a book with multiple descriptive characters
Example: 'the old man' and 'the detective' are different people
Verify they remain as separate character entries
Check that context/chapter distribution is used to distinguish
Confirm no incorrect merging of distinct descriptive characters
Run analysis on a book with epithet variations
Verify canonical name is most specific (e.g., 'the blind old man' over 'the old man')
Check that less specific forms appear as aliases
Confirm canonical selection follows: specificity > uniqueness > frequency

changes.description: Add EPITHET_ALIAS_PROMPT for semantic equivalence detection
Add _is_descriptive_handle() to detect 'the X' style handles
Separate proper names from descriptive handles, run epithet resolution on descriptive group

features.name: Verification Gate
features.rationale: Catch pronoun entries that slipped through and flag missing high-frequency agentive descriptions as a safety net.
features.current_behavior: Verification checks for duplicates but not pronouns or missing agentive descriptions
features.proposed_behavior: Add verification checks that: (1) hard-fail pronoun/determiner entries, (2) scan for high-frequency agentive descriptions missing from character list

user_stories.description: Pronoun entries are flagged and auto-removed
steps: Run analysis (with potential mention matching bugs)
Check verification output
Verify pronoun entries are flagged as errors
Check that refine() auto-removes pronoun entries
Confirm final character list contains no pronouns
Run analysis on a book with unnamed agentive character
Check verification output
Verify warning if 'the X said/walked/etc' appears 10+ times but not in character list
Check that suggested fix recommends adding as character or alias
Confirm scan uses agentive verb patterns (said, walked, grabbed, etc.)

changes.description: Add _check_missing_agentive_descriptions() - scan text for high-frequency 'the X said' patterns
Auto-remove pronoun entries based on error-severity issues

features.name: Coreference Resolution
features.rationale: Link pronouns back to specific characters to boost mention counts and provide pronoun-to-character mappings. Enhancement, not critical path.
features.proposed_behavior: Add CoreferenceProposer using spaCy coreference (spacy-experimental or coreferee) that links pronouns to antecedent noun phrases

user_stories.description: Pronoun coreferences boost character mention counts
steps: Run analysis with coreference enabled
Examine character mention counts
Verify characters with many pronoun references have boosted counts
Check that pronoun references are linked to correct character
Confirm coreference proposer gracefully degrades if not available

files.description: NEW FILE: CoreferenceProposer class using spaCy coreference

changes.description: Add CoreferenceProposer to proposer list if available
